question.text: Will the U.S. Trustee's official committee of unsecured creditors in The Children's Place Chapter 11 case have seven or more members as of November 27, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves by counting the members named in the most recent notice of appointment of an official committee of unsecured creditors filed by the United States Trustee with a filing date on or before November 27, 2026 on the docket of In re The Children's Place, Inc., et al., Case No. 26-22682 (SLM) (Bankr. D.N.J.). The docket to be used is the case docket published by the Debtors' claims and noticing agent, Omni Agent Solutions, at https://cases.omniagentsolutions.com/documents?clientid=3814. The question resolves YES if that notice names seven or more committee members, and NO if it names six or fewer. If no such notice has a filing date of November 27, 2026 or earlier, the question resolves NO. If that docket is unavailable or incomplete, the court's own docket (via PACER) or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used instead.
question.fine_print: Professionals, counsel, financial advisors and other non-member parties named in the notice do not count as members; only entities designated as members of the committee count. Whether the November 27, 2026 cutoff is met is determined by the filing date shown on the docket entry, not by the date the entry was entered on the docket or first displayed online.

research:
I found no notice of a U.S. Trustee creditors' committee in this case so far. Nothing settles the question yet, and I could not see the deciding docket directly.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16: The Omni Agent Solutions docket page (clientid=3814) and the case home page both return HTTP 403 Forbidden to my tools, so I could not read the deciding docket. I also have no PACER access. [Omni](https://cases.omniagentsolutions.com/documents?clientid=3814)
- 2026-11-10: The latest committee status I can confirm comes from the interim DIP order (Docket No. 66). It says the U.S. Trustee "has not yet appointed" a committee. This is the same fact given in your background, repeated in secondary summaries. [Bondoro](https://bondoro.com/the-childrens-place/)
- I found no committee notice on the U.S. Trustee's website (justice.gov) for case 26-22682. The New Jersey U.S. Trustee office does post its committee solicitation letters for 2026 cases there. [DOJ example](https://justice.gov/ust/media/1460566/dl?inline=)

## 2. Current status
- I found no evidence that a committee notice has been filed as of 2026-11-16. Nothing settles the question yet.
- 2026-11-13: A Chapter11Cases write-up lists no committee and puts the section 341 creditors' meeting on December 17, 2026. That meeting is not a deadline for appointing the committee. [Chapter11Cases](https://chapter11cases.com/blogs/news/the-children-s-place-in-chapter-11-a-fleetwide-liquidation-with-a-going-concern-exit-ramp)
- The interim DIP order gives a future committee a $50,000 budget to investigate the lenders' liens. It also sets a 60-day challenge period from committee formation; if no committee forms, the deadline is January 25, 2027. [Bondoro](https://bondoro.com/the-childrens-place/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-13: Patch and Octus covered the filing and sale process. Neither mentions a committee. [Patch](https://patch.com/maryland/across-md/beloved-clothing-store-files-bankruptcy-putting-md-locations-risk), [Octus](https://octus.com/resources/articles/case-summary-gymboree-brand-owner-retailer-the-childrens-place-files-ch-11-proposing-dual-track-process-reports-considerable-interest-from-prospective-buyers/)
- 2026-11-12: The bidding procedures order was entered. It sends expense invoices to the U.S. Trustee and "any statutory committee." [Bondoro APA summary](https://app.bondoro.com/preview/cases/The_Childrens_Place_Inc/apa-summary)
- 2026-11-09/10: WWD reported on how much the company owes apparel suppliers, led by Hansae at about $15.4 million. That makes a large pool of trade creditors who could serve on a committee. [WWD](https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/childrens-place-bankruptcy-apparel-suppliers-hansae-1239409777/)
- 2026-11-08: Petition date. [White & Case](https://www.whitecase.com/news/press-release/white-case-represents-childrens-place-inc-chapter-11-proceedings-address-more)

## 4. Base rates
- U.S. Trustee solicitation letters say a committee "ordinarily" consists of the holders of the seven largest unsecured claims who are willing to serve, with a minimum of three. [DOJ](https://justice.gov/ust/media/1460566/dl?inline=)
- Rite Aid's 2025 case in the same New Jersey court: petition on May 5, 2025, a nine-member committee appointed on May 16, 2025 (11 days later), and the committee reconstituted on May 19. That is one New Jersey retail case with 7 or more members, appointed in about 11 days. [Law360](https://www.law360.com/bankruptcy-authority/amp/articles/2341368)
- Liberated Brands, a 2025 apparel retailer case (court not confirmed): seven members, including landlords and vendors. [Law360](https://www.law360.com/bankruptcy-authority/articles/2300150/creditors-committee-tapped-in-liberated-brands-ch-11)
- Timing: committees in large Region 3 cases (the U.S. Trustee region covering New Jersey and Delaware) are typically appointed 7 to 14 days after filing. That rule of thumb is my own general knowledge; I did not find a source for it. On that pace, an appointment would fall around November 15-22, before the effective November 25 cutoff. Liquidation and sale cases sometimes get smaller committees of 3 to 5 members, or none if creditors are unwilling to serve. I did not find a systematic dataset of committee sizes in New Jersey cases.
- Apparel suppliers based outside the U.S., such as Hansae (Korea) and TNG (Vietnam), may be less willing to serve, which could shrink the committee. Landlords and service vendors often fill seats in retail cases.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the prediction market prices supplied (Kalshi, Polymarket) match this question. The closest, Kalshi's 2026 bankruptcy count, is unrelated. I found nothing on Manifold or Metaculus specific to this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Now through November 25: a U.S. Trustee committee formation meeting and notice of appointment could come at any time; this is the key event. The Trustee could also file an amended notice adding or removing members, and the most recent notice filed by November 27 is the one that counts.
- 2026-11-17: Proposed deadline to designate stalking horse bidders. [Bondoro](https://bondoro.com/the-childrens-place/)
- 2026-11-20: DIP loan deadline for motions related to the Fort Payne distribution center. [Bondoro](https://bondoro.com/the-childrens-place/)
- 2026-11-23, 9:30 a.m. ET: Status conference. Committee formation may come up there.
- 2026-11-26: Thanksgiving, courts closed. In practice the last filing day is November 25.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) Time left and what is needed for Yes: about 9 working days remain. Because of Thanksgiving, the last practical filing day is November 25, 2026. For Yes, the U.S. Trustee must file a notice appointing an unsecured creditors' committee with a filing date of November 27 or earlier, and the most recent such notice must name at least seven members.

(b) Status quo: no committee has been appointed as of docket entry 110 (November 12), and nothing found as of November 16. If nothing changed, the question resolves No.

(c) Base rate: the outcome needs two things to happen.
- **Appointment by November 25:** In large Region 3 and New Jersey retail cases, the U.S. Trustee usually appoints a committee 7 to 14 days after filing. Examples are Rite Aid at 11 days and Bed Bath & Beyond at about 9 days. A 17-day window covers most such cases, so I put this at about 80-85%.
- **Seven or more members:** Large retail cases with many vendors and mall landlords often get seven to nine members. Examples are Rite Aid with nine and Liberated Brands with seven. Liquidations and cases dominated by foreign vendors sometimes get only three to five. I put this at about 50-55% if a committee is appointed.
- **Combined:** roughly 40-45%.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - The case is large: $881M in liabilities and $93.9M of top-30 trade debt.
  - There are many potential members, including mall landlords such as Simon and Brookfield, service vendors and apparel makers.
  - U.S. Trustee solicitation letters say a committee "ordinarily" consists of the seven largest unsecured claimants willing to serve.
  - In Rite Aid (D.N.J., May 2025), a nine-member committee was appointed 11 days after filing.
- **For No:**
  - No committee existed as of November 12-16.
  - The largest creditors are foreign (Hansae in Korea, TNG in Vietnam) and may not be willing to serve.
  - This is a fast liquidation and sale, which can produce a smaller committee.
  - The holiday shortens the filing window.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** The U.S. Trustee holds a formation meeting around November 18-20. Few foreign vendors respond, and the Trustee appoints five members: two vendors, two landlords and one logistics provider. Alternatively, the appointment slips past Thanksgiving.
- **Yes:** Around November 19, the Trustee appoints seven members: three apparel vendors including Hansae, two mall REITs, a freight or logistics company and a service vendor.

(f) Adjustment: I start from about 45%. I trim slightly for the unconfirmed timing and for the liquidation and foreign-vendor profile, which points toward a smaller committee. There is no matching prediction market to anchor on.
